timeline.event: Work and community engagement requirements begin for MAGI New Adult Group (Aid Code M1)
Six-month renewals begin (was annual). Exempt populations remain annual.
Multi-state lawsuit filed: California v. Mehmet Oz challenging IFR provisions
DHCS HR1 Implementation Plan webinar released
DHCS MEDIL I26-25 outreach letter template to members

who_subject: Adults 19-64 enrolled under MAGI New Adult Group (ACA expansion). Estimated 4.8M Californians in this category as of May 2026 (DHCS).
who_not_subject: People with disabilities / medically frail / serious health condition / SUD
People on Medicare Part A or B

qualifying_activities.detail: Monthly gross income before taxes >= $580. Seasonal/fluctuating: average >=$580 over prior 6 months. Includes wages, self-employment net, unemployment, SSDI, retirement, dividends, rental net, etc.
Paid employment, self-employment, gig work. Includes all jobs.
Enrolled at least half-time in educational or career/technical education program. Less than half-time can combine hours to reach 80.
Any mix of above totaling >=80 hrs/month, or income equivalent

how_verified: Counties must first check ex parte via existing data (employment, income, program participation). If not verifiable, enrollee gets notice and 30 days to provide documentation. Renewal frequency changes to every 6 months for M1 population at next renewal after Jan 1, 2027.

coverage_loss_estimates.estimate: 1.1M lose coverage by 2029-30 due to work requirement
233K by June 2027, 1M by Jan 2028, 1.4M by June 2028

california_mitigation: Ex parte verification via existing state data before asking enrollee
Implement ALL optional short-term hardship exemptions (emergency, high unemployment county, inpatient care, medical travel)
Outreach letters at least 3 months before first look-back period (MEDIL I26-25 template)
Lead plaintiff in multi-state lawsuit Commonwealth of Massachusetts et al. v. Mehmet Oz (June 2026) challenging IFR
Counties instructed to accept multiple forms of verification
About $1.3B General Fund reflected in the enacted 2026-27 budget for H.R.1-related Medi-Cal costs (the $1.1B January figure was not H.R.1 implementation funding)
